full_judgment: 7. I have perused the judgment of the trial court as well as that of the appellate court and also the application under Section-115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I have, also examined the evidence, oral and documentary on record. It is not disputed that opposite party No. 1 is a stranger to the holding. Opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 transferred 181 shatak out of 53 shatak of land of plot No. 443 appertaining to khatian No. 705 to opposite party No. 1 by a deed of sale executed on 20.03.73. The sale deed was duly registered on 13.07.77 the application under Section-96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption was made on 14.09.77. The petitioners are co-sharers in the holding. So their application for pre-emption was rightly held by the trial court not barred by limitation. They are also entitled to get the land pre-empted as the petitioners had 8/10 bighas of land only in total.
